due_when.clears_when: Next phase, Tier-3. Design first, in this order: (1) pct-per-leg against each leg's own size, never a shared qty; (2) per-leg cumulative-partial state, with a leg reaching 100% closing THAT LEG and the package draining exactly as the full-close path now does; (3) a non-idempotent partial-application story — a retry must not re-reduce a leg that already succeeded, which rules out copying the full-close path's blanket 'leave it and retry next tick'. Likely needs a per-leg applied-marker keyed on (package, leg, verdict instance). Then: tests pinning unequal leg sizes (use the measured 149.5-vs-48,625.8 XRP shape), a partial that lands on one leg and fails on another, and a leg crossing 100% while a sibling does not. DONE when all three effectuation branches resolve legs through `_package_open_legs` and no branch is silently single-leg. Also worth measuring on the way in (cheap, and it sizes the backlog): has a partial-close verdict ever fired on a multi-leg package? — packages with >1 trade row whose legs' position_size diverges from entry size.
